summary: Packers Peak cupola-style lookout, Klamath National Forest: planned 1913, built 1914 per the register, staffed seasonally into the 1930s; nothing remains on the site.

facts.design: Cupola-style lookout cabin (register); the 1913 plan was a 12 by 12 house under an eight-foot octagonal glass tower
facts.status_note: Nothing remains at the site, according to the register; removal date unknown.

staffing.status: seasonal lookouts named in newspapers, 1916 to 1930

facts.agency: US Forest Service - Klamath National Forest

events.note: Register: the site was a lookout site as early as 1911, with the lookout using a nearby cabin
Newspaper: three new lookout houses planned in July 1913; this one expected ready by August 1
Register: cupola-style lookout cabin built in 1914
Telephone line between Cecilville and the lookout completed in October 1914
Fire on Coffee Creek, reported by the lookout, burned about 300 acres
Jacob Leschinski stationed as lookout; again noted in 1923
Sand and cement hauled for a cabin foundation for the lookout; the chronology notes the cabin was actually at Big Bend Meadow
Henry Duvol named lookout for the 1930 season

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register gives 1914 for the cupola-style cabin. The July 1913 newspaper item expected the new house ready by August 1, 1913, and a telephone line to the lookout was completed in October 1914. The story gives both dates and does not choose one.

notes_for_editor: Built year conflicts: the register says 1914, the July 1913 newspaper expected occupancy by August 1, 1913, and the telephone line was finished October 1914. The 1926 chronology entry says the cabin was actually at Big Bend Meadow, but the register says a nearby cabin was used early on; the story does not reconcile these. The Forest Lookouts chronology stops in 1931, so the register's 'served into the 1960s' is not confirmed by the sources read. Staffing names are from newspaper items only. Access and current condition not found; the register says nothing remains. One WebSearch returned hiking and peak-listing pages plus a lead to a 1958 Klamath National Forest lookout eligibility study, which was not read. No new photos; the record's Nancy Hood photo is already in the record.
